text: A few weeks of real weekly scoring go by. Tom Bellamy's team starts noticing the risk scores aren't actually catching the accounts that don't renew.
Felix and Grace investigate, and the trail leads back to Lesson 13's SHAP plot: why did the model lean so heavily on just logins_last_30d and days_since_last_login?
The answer is in the original training SQL: those features were computed relative to COALESCE(ChurnDate, CURRENT_DATE) -- for a churned account, that's the day it already left, not today.
An honest, time-consistent backtest -- scoring accounts exactly the way production does, with no future knowledge -- puts the real AUC at about 0.74, not 0.98.
The leak is understood. It isn't fixed yet.
